'''Shigeru Iitaka''' (飯高 茂 Iitaka Shigeru, born May 29, 1942, [[Chiba (city)|Chiba]]) is a Japanese mathematician at [[Gakushuin University]] working in algebraic geometry who introduced the [[Kodaira dimension]], and [[Iitaka dimension]]. He was a world leader in the field of [[Algebraic geometry]].

He received his Ph.D. in 1970 from the [[University of Tokyo]] under [[Kunihiko Kodaira]] with thesis「代数多様体のD-次元について」(''On D-dimensions of algebraic varieties'').<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=188665}}</ref> He was awarded the Iyanaga Prize of the [[Mathematical Society of Japan]] in 1980 and the [[Japan Academy Prize (academics)|Japan Academy Prize]] in 1990.
